requirements.title: The topic tree and the life of a topic in it
requirements.rationale: A broad topic can only be divided when a topic can sit under another one.

criteria.action: allow a link to be filed under a topic at any level, including a topic that has child topics
keep the owner's topic names unique ignoring case, whatever the place of each topic in the tree, refusing a rename to a name that a topic elsewhere in the tree has
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 {error: 'name_taken', message} for the rename; the topic keeps its name

setup: the owner has a top-level topic 'Languages' with a child topic 'Rust', and a top-level topic 'Systems', each with a link
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts, extend 'refuses a name another topic or tag has, changing nothing' with the case of a top-level topic renamed to the name of a child elsewhere in the tree: r = PATCH /api/v1/topics/{Systems} {name: 'rust'}; assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error == 'name_taken'; assert the topic is still named 'Systems' and 'Rust' is still under 'Languages'

criteria.condition: a link's topic is changed or the link is deleted, and the topic it left has no link filed directly under it and no child topic
criteria.action: delete that topic, then delete its parent when the parent is left with no link filed directly under it and no child topic, and so on up to the top level

setup: the owner has a chain 'A' > 'B' > 'C' (parent_id set in the topics table) and one link filed under 'C'
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts, extend the table of 'a topic or tag whose last link loses it is gone' with rows over the chain: {editing the link's topic to 'Other' -> A, B and C gone}, {deleting the link -> A, B and C gone}, {decay removing the link -> A, B and C gone}, {the same three writes when 'A' also has a link of its own -> B and C gone, A kept}, {when 'B' has a second child 'D' with a link -> only C gone}; assert the remaining topics by reading the topics table

requirements.title: Listing the topics with their place in the tree
requirements.rationale: The website and scripts need each topic's parent and both of its counts to show the tree.

criteria.condition: a client sends GET /api/v1/topics
criteria.action: return every topic of the owner, whether or not a link is filed directly under it, each with its parent, the number of links filed directly under it, the number of links filed under it or any topic beneath it, and the added date of the newest of those links
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 {items: [{id, name, parent_id: string | null, count, subtree_count, newest_added_at}], next_cursor}; parent_id is null for a top-level topic; count counts the links filed directly under the topic in any state; subtree_count counts the links filed under it or any topic beneath it in any state; newest_added_at is the newest added_at among those links; items are ordered by newest_added_at descending, then id descending; no other user's topic is listed

setup: the owner has 'A' (one expired link added 2026-01-01) > 'B' (no link of its own) > 'C' (links added 2026-01-03 and 2026-01-05), and a top-level 'D' (one link added 2026-01-04)
another user has a topic of their own
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts, give the topics row of '$route lists each with its count and newest link, newest first' this tree: r = GET /api/v1/topics; assert by name: A {parent_id: null, count: 1, subtree_count: 3, newest_added_at: '2026-01-05...'}, B {parent_id: A.id, count: 0, subtree_count: 2, newest_added_at: '2026-01-05...'}, C {parent_id: B.id, count: 2, subtree_count: 2, newest_added_at: '2026-01-05...'}, D {parent_id: null, count: 1, subtree_count: 1, newest_added_at: '2026-01-04...'}; assert the items are sorted by (newest_added_at desc, id desc) and the other user's topic is absent

criteria.condition: a topic has no link filed directly under it and has at least one child topic
criteria.action: keep the topic and list it in GET /api/v1/topics with count 0
criteria.contract: the topic's item has count 0 and subtree_count equal to the links beneath it

setup: the owner has 'A' with one link and a child 'B' with one link
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts beside the test of REQ-1.3: PATCH the link under 'A' to the topic 'Other'; r = GET /api/v1/topics; assert 'A' is listed with {count: 0, subtree_count: 1} and 'B' is still its child

criteria.action: page GET /api/v1/topics with limit and cursor as before, newest link first, so that every topic, a parent sharing its newest link with its child included, is listed exactly once across pages

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts, extend '$route pages with the cursor' for /api/v1/topics with a tree of five topics in which a parent and its only child share their newest link: page with limit=2 to the end; assert every topic name appears exactly once, in (newest_added_at desc, id desc) order, and a forged cursor still answers invalid_cursor

criteria.action: return the items of GET /api/v1/tags exactly as before, each as {id, name, count, newest_added_at} without parent_id or subtree_count

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts, keep the tags row of '$route lists each with its count and newest link, newest first' asserting the exact item objects {name, count, newest_added_at} (ids aside), so that an extra key fails it

requirements.title: A link's topic path and the exported tree
requirements.rationale: Every reader of a link, the website and agents alike, needs to know where its topic sits without loading the whole tree.

criteria.action: return on every link it returns, alone or in a list, a topic_path holding the names of the topics from the link's top-level topic down to its own topic, beside topic holding the name of its own topic
criteria.contract: topic_path: string[] ([] when the link has no topic); topic: string | null, equal to the last element of topic_path

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/links/links.test.ts, extend 'reading a link' with a table over the three links: assert GET /api/v1/links/{id} gives {topic: null, topic_path: []}, {topic: 'A', topic_path: ['A']} and {topic: 'C', topic_path: ['A', 'B', 'C']}; assert GET /api/v1/links (the stream) and GET /api/v1/search?q=topic:A give the same topic_path for the same links

criteria.condition: the owner downloads GET /api/v1/export
criteria.action: give each topic in the export's topics its parent_id beside its id, name and link_count
criteria.contract: topics: [{id, name, parent_id: string | null, link_count}], link_count counting the links filed directly under the topic

setup: the owner has 'A' (one link) > 'B' (two links)
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/account/export.test.ts, extend 'gives workspaces their links in order, and topics and tags their counts': assert doc.topics equals [{id: A.id, name: 'A', parent_id: null, link_count: 1}, {id: B.id, name: 'B', parent_id: A.id, link_count: 2}]

requirements.title: Moving a topic
requirements.rationale: The owner arranges the tree by placing a topic, with everything beneath it, under another one or at the top.

criteria.condition: a client sends POST /api/v1/topics/{id}/move with {"parent": "<topic id>"} or {"parent": null}, both topics being the owner's, and the move leaves every topic at level 3 or above
criteria.action: make the topic a child of the named parent, or a top-level topic for null, moving every topic beneath it along with it
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 {id, name, parent_id, count, subtree_count} of the moved topic; the parent_id of every topic beneath it is unchanged

setup: the owner has 'Languages' > 'Rust' > 'Async', a top-level 'Programming' and a top-level 'Systems', each topic with one link
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts, a new describe 'moving a topic' with a table: {move 'Systems' under 'Programming' -> Systems.parent_id == Programming.id}, {move 'Rust' to null -> Rust top-level, 'Async' still under 'Rust'}, {move 'Async' under 'Programming' -> Async at level 2}, {move 'Rust' under 'Systems' -> 'Rust' at level 2 and 'Async' at level 3 under it}; for each: r = POST /api/v1/topics/{id}/move {parent}; assert r.status == 200 and r.json == {id, name, parent_id, count, subtree_count} of the topic; assert GET /api/v1/topics shows the expected parent_id of every topic

criteria.condition: the move would put the topic or any topic beneath it at level 4 or below
criteria.action: refuse the move and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 {error: 'too_deep', message: 'topics are at most three levels deep'}; every topic's parent_id and every link's updated_at are unchanged

setup: the owner has 'Languages' > 'Rust' > 'Async', a top-level 'Programming' with a child 'Tools', each topic with one link, and another user has a topic 'Theirs'
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts in 'moving a topic', one table of refusals, each followed by asserting that GET /api/v1/topics and every link are as before: {'Languages' under 'Programming' -> 409 too_deep}, {'Programming' under 'Rust' -> 409 too_deep}, {'Languages' under 'Async' -> 409 invalid_move 'a topic cannot move under itself'}, {'Rust' under 'Rust' -> 409 invalid_move}, {body {} -> 400 invalid_move field parent}, {body {parent: 42} -> 400 invalid_move field parent}, {body {parent: ''} -> 400 invalid_move field parent}, {parent 'Theirs' -> 404 not_found}, {topic id 'Theirs' -> 404 not_found}, {unknown topic id -> 404 not_found}; assert r.status and r.json against the case

criteria.condition: the new parent is the topic itself or a topic beneath it
criteria.action: refuse the move and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 {error: 'invalid_move', message: 'a topic cannot move under itself'}; every topic's parent_id is unchanged

criteria.condition: the body has no parent key, or parent is neither null nor a non-empty string
criteria.action: refuse the move and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 {error: 'invalid_move', field: 'parent', message: string}

criteria.condition: the topic or the named parent is not one of the owner's topics
criteria.action: refuse the move and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 {error: 'not_found'}

criteria.condition: a client moves a topic under the parent it already has, or a top-level topic to null
criteria.action: answer as a move answers and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 {id, name, parent_id, count, subtree_count}; no topic and no link's updated_at changes

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts in 'moving a topic': for {'Rust' under 'Languages'} and {'Programming' to null}: before = read every link's updated_at; r = POST move; assert r.status == 200 and r.json.parent_id is unchanged; assert every link's updated_at equals before

criteria.condition: a move leaves the topic's former parent with no link filed directly under it and no child topic
criteria.action: delete the former parent, and each ancestor left the same way, up to the top level

setup: the owner has 'A' > 'B' > 'C' where only 'C' has a link, and a top-level 'D' with a link
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts in 'moving a topic': POST /api/v1/topics/{C}/move {parent: D}; assert GET /api/v1/topics lists exactly 'D' and 'C' with C.parent_id == D.id, 'A' and 'B' being gone

requirements.title: Merging and renaming topics in the tree
requirements.rationale: Merge and Rename are how the owner corrects the tree, so they have to keep it whole.

criteria.condition: a client merges a topic that has child topics into another of the owner's topics with POST /api/v1/topics/{id}/merge, and the merge leaves every topic at level 3 or above
criteria.action: make the source's children children of the survivor, with their own children beneath them, then give the source's links to the survivor and delete the source
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 {id, name, count} of the survivor; every former child of the source has parent_id equal to the survivor's id; the source's name is an alias of the survivor

setup: the owner has 'Rustlang' (one link) > 'Async' (one link) > 'Tokio' (one link), and a top-level 'Rust' (one link)
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts in 'merging topics and tags', beside 'gives every link of a topic the survivor, and carries its aliases over': r = POST /api/v1/topics/{Rustlang}/merge {into: Rust}; assert r.status == 200 and r.json == {id: Rust.id, name: 'Rust', count: 2}; assert GET /api/v1/topics gives Async.parent_id == Rust.id and Tokio.parent_id == Async.id and no 'Rustlang'

criteria.condition: a merge would put any topic at level 4 or below
criteria.action: refuse the merge and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 {error: 'too_deep', message: 'topics are at most three levels deep'}; the source, its links, its children and every parent_id are unchanged

setup: the owner has 'Languages' > 'Rust' > 'Async', and 'Programming' > 'Tools', each topic with one link
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts in 'merging topics and tags', one table of refusals, each followed by asserting that GET /api/v1/topics and every link's topic are as before: {merge 'Rust' (which has the child 'Async') into 'Tools' -> 409 too_deep}, {merge 'Languages' into 'Async' -> 409 invalid_merge 'a topic cannot merge into a topic beneath it'}, {merge 'Languages' into 'Rust' -> 409 invalid_merge}

criteria.condition: the survivor of a merge is beneath the source
criteria.action: refuse the merge and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 {error: 'invalid_merge', message: 'a topic cannot merge into a topic beneath it'}; the source, its links and every parent_id are unchanged

criteria.condition: a merge leaves the source's former parent with no link filed directly under it and no child topic
criteria.action: delete the former parent, and each ancestor left the same way, up to the top level

setup: the owner has 'A' > 'B' where only 'B' has a link, and a top-level 'C' with a link
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts in 'merging topics and tags': POST /api/v1/topics/{B}/merge {into: C}; assert GET /api/v1/topics lists exactly 'C', with both links

criteria.condition: a client renames a topic with PATCH /api/v1/topics/{id} to a valid name
criteria.action: keep the topic's parent and its children
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 {id, name, count}; the topic's parent_id and its children's parent_id are unchanged

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/search/vocabulary.test.ts in 'renaming a topic or tag': r = PATCH /api/v1/topics/{Rust} {name: 'Rust language'}; assert r.status == 200; assert GET /api/v1/topics gives 'Rust language' parent_id == Languages.id and Async.parent_id == Rust.id

criteria.condition: the new name of a topic holds the character >
criteria.action: refuse the rename and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 {error: 'invalid_name', field: 'name', message: 'a topic name of 1 to 100 characters, without >'}; the topic keeps its name

requirements.title: Searching the tree and keeping the indexes current
requirements.rationale: A search for a broad topic must still find what has been filed beneath it, and a rearranged tree must be found where it now is.

criteria.condition: a query holds the filter topic:<name> and <name> is, ignoring case, the name of one of the owner's topics
criteria.action: match every link filed under that topic or under any topic beneath it, and no other link
criteria.contract: the results of GET /api/v1/search hold exactly those links; a name that is only an alias of a topic matches no link

criteria.action: match a free word of a search against every name in a link's topic_path, in the topic column of the word index, with the topic column's weight

criteria.contract: a word of the new name finds those links and a word only of the old name finds none; INDEX_QUEUE receives one message for each of those links

criteria.contract: GET /api/v1/links?changed_since=<a time before the merge> returns exactly those links; a word of the survivor's name finds them and a word only of the source's name finds none; INDEX_QUEUE receives one message for each of them

requirements.title: Setting a link's topic by a typed path
requirements.rationale: Typing a path files a link and creates the sub-topic it belongs to in one edit.

criteria.condition: a client sends PATCH /api/v1/links/{id} with topic holding one name or two or three names separated by >
criteria.action: resolve the names from the first, each trimmed of surrounding spaces with inner spaces collapsed: a name equal, ignoring case, to one of the owner's topic names or topic aliases uses that topic (the alias's survivor); any other name, near names included, is created as typed under the topic the name before it resolved to, or at the top level for the first name; then file the link under the topic the last name resolved to and record topic as edited
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the link: topic equal to the last resolved topic's name, topic_path its path from the top level, edited_fields holding 'topic'

setup: the owner has 'Software engineering' > 'Testing' > 'Fuzzing' (each with a link), a top-level 'Cooking', an alias 'SE' of 'Software engineering', and a link to edit
check.pseudocode: in src/worker/enrich/edits.test.ts, a table in 'editing a link': {'Gardening' -> new top-level, path ['Gardening']}, {'software ENGINEERING' -> filed under the existing topic that has children, path ['Software engineering']}, {'Software engineering > Unit tests' -> 'Unit tests' created under it}, {'Hobbies > Woodwork > Joinery' -> all three created, path of three}, {'SE > Mocks' -> 'Mocks' created under 'Software engineering'}, {'Testings' -> a new top-level 'Testings', no near match}, {'  Software engineering>Testing  ' -> path ['Software engineering', 'Testing']}, {'Cooking > Testing' -> filed under the existing 'Testing' where it is: path ['Software engineering', 'Testing'], Testing's parent unchanged, no second 'Testing'}, {'Cooking > Testing > Mutation' -> 'Mutation' created under 'Testing'}, {'Fuzzing > Corpus' -> 'Corpus' created under 'Testing', the parent of the level-3 'Fuzzing', path ['Software engineering', 'Testing', 'Corpus']}; for each: r = PATCH {topic}; assert r.status == 200, r.json.topic, r.json.topic_path and edited_fields; assert the topics table holds no two names equal ignoring case

criteria.condition: a name of a typed path matches an existing topic that sits under another parent, or at another level, than the path puts it
criteria.action: use that topic where it is, without moving it, and resolve the next name of the path under it
criteria.contract: the existing topic's parent_id is unchanged and no second topic with its name exists

criteria.condition: a new name of a typed path would be created at level 4, because the name before it matched an existing level-3 topic
criteria.action: create the new topic under the parent of that level-3 topic and file the link under it
criteria.contract: the new topic's parent_id is the level-3 topic's parent_id; the link's topic_path has three names

criteria.condition: the topic of the edit is a path of more than three names, or holds an empty name, or a name longer than 100 characters
criteria.action: refuse the whole edit and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 {error: 'invalid_topic', field: 'topic', message: 'a topic or a path of up to three topics separated by >, each 1 to 100 characters'}; no topic is created and the link is as it was

check.pseudocode: in src/worker/enrich/edits.test.ts, extend the table of 'refuses $body whole' with {topic: 'A > B > C > D'}, {topic: 'A > > B'}, {topic: 'A >'}, {topic: '> A'}, {topic: 'A > ' + 't'.repeat(101)}, keeping {topic: ''} and {topic: 't'.repeat(101)}; assert r.json == {error: 'invalid_topic', field: 'topic', message: 'a topic or a path of up to three topics separated by >, each 1 to 100 characters'}, the link equals what it was and the topics table holds no new row

requirements.title: Carrying existing topics over to the tree
requirements.rationale: The owner's existing library must arrive in the tree unchanged, and > must be free to separate a path's names.

criteria.condition: the topic tree migration is applied to a database that holds topics

criteria.contract: every topic has parent_id null; every link's topic_id is the one it had, unless its topic was merged by REQ-10.3

criteria.condition: the topic tree migration finds a topic whose name holds >
criteria.action: replace every > in the name with -, and keep the former name as an alias of the topic
criteria.contract: the topic's name has each > replaced by -; topic_aliases holds the former name for the topic

criteria.condition: a name with > replaced by - is already another topic's name of the same owner, ignoring case
criteria.action: merge the topic into that other topic as a merge does: give it the topic's links, keep the topic's former name and aliases as aliases of it, and delete the topic
criteria.contract: the other topic holds the links; the former name is its alias; the renamed topic no longer exists
